title: Legislative districts of Zamboanga del Norte
wikitext:
{{Politics of the Philippines}} {{short description|Philippine political representations}} The '''legislative districts of Zamboanga del Norte''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Zamboanga del Norte]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[Zamboanga del Norte's 1st congressional district|first]], [[Zamboanga del Norte's 2nd congressional district|second]] and [[Zamboanga del Norte's 3rd congressional district|third]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Zamboanga}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Zamboanga del Norte were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and the historical [[Zamboanga (province)|Zamboanga Province]] (1935–1953). The enactment of Republic Act No. 711 on June 6, 1952 divided the old Zamboanga Province into [[Zamboanga del Norte]] and [[Zamboanga del Sur]] and provided them each with a congressional representative.{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 711 – An Act to Create the Provinces of Zamboanga del Norte and Zamboanga del Sur|author=Congress of the Philippines|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/8_republicacts.php?id=715 |website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=November 27, 2017|date=June 6, 1952}} Zamboanga del Norte first elected its separate representative starting in the [[1953 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1953 elections]]. Even after receiving their own city charters, [[Dapitan]] and [[Dipolog]] remained part of the representation of the Province of Zamboanga del Norte by virtue of Section 80 of Republic Act No. 3811 (June 22, 1963){{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 3811 – An Act Creating the City of Dapitan|url=https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1963/ra_3811_1963.html|website=The LawPhil Project|access-date=November 28, 2017|date=June 22, 1963}} and Section 86 of Republic Act No. 5520 (June 21, 1969),{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 5520 – An Act Creating the City of Dipolog|url=https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1969/ra_5520_1969.html|website= The LawPhil Project|access-date=November 28, 2017|date=June 21, 1969}} respectively. Zamboanga del Norte was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IX]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|two representatives, elected at-large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province was reapportioned into three congressional districts;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines – Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} each elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == Current districts == Zamboanga del Norte's current congressional delegation is composed of three members. {{Color box|{{party color|Lakas-Christian Muslim Democrats}}|border=darkgray}} [[Lakas–CMD]] (2)
